sourcedFrom: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: This book carries the 1100 and the 11-87 side by side and every procedure here comes from a section headed Model 11-87 — the 11-87 adds a gas cylinder collar the 1100 does not have, and its piston stack forks three ways by gauge and chambering. Routine cleaning is barrel and gas parts off the magazine tube; taking the action bars, breech bolt and trigger plate out is the deeper procedure in the Deep Clean branch.

steps.title: Cross-bolt safety in, red band out of sight
steps.action: Push the safety button behind the trigger until the RED BAND MARKING cannot be seen, keeping your finger outside the trigger guard while you move it.
steps.prose: The 11-87 safety is a cross-bolt button through the rear of the trigger guard and it reports by colour: red showing means the gun will fire when the trigger is pulled. Push it through from the side that hides the band and confirm by eye, because a button that has not gone fully across can still leave a sliver of red. It stays engaged through the whole strip on this gun — the trigger plate removal later depends on it.
steps.quote: The safety mechanism on the Model 1100/11-87 Shotguns is a button located behind the trigger. See Pictures 3 and 4.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Important Parts of the Firearm — The Safety Mechanism, p.7
steps.warn: Remington: the firearm will fire when the trigger is pulled and the RED BAND IS SHOWING.

steps.title: An 1100 barrel is not an 11-87 barrel — check the marking
steps.action: Read the model marking on the receiver and on the barrel and confirm you have an 11-87 barrel on an 11-87 receiver before anything comes apart.
steps.prose: Remington prints this prohibition five times in one 26-page book because the two barrels mount identically on the magazine tube and are not interchangeable — the gas port and barrel extension are matched to different gas systems. Put an 1100 barrel on an 11-87 and the gun either short-strokes or runs at pressures the parts were not built for. This is a bench-time hazard as much as a purchase-time one: two similar barrels out of their receivers on the same table is exactly how the wrong one goes back on.
steps.quote: WARNING: MODEL 11-87™ BARRELS CAN NOT BE USED AS REPLACEMENT BARRELS ON MODEL 1100 FIREARMS. MODEL 1100 BARRELS CAN NOT BE USED AS REPLACEMENT BARRELS ON MODEL 11-87 FIREARMS.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Assemble (Model 11-87™) — warning under the heading, p.11

steps.title: Is the receiver marked SUPER MAGNUM? That changes the parts
steps.action: Read the receiver marking. If it says MODEL 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM, the gun takes only 3 1⁄2" chambered 12-gauge 11-87 barrels, has no gas cylinder collar, and carries a barrel seal activator in the piston stack.
steps.prose: The Super Magnum is a separate variant inside this one book and it is the fork that decides what actually slides off the magazine tube in a few steps' time. Never fit a 12-gauge 11-87 barrel with a chamber shorter than 3 1⁄2" to a receiver marked Super Magnum, and do not go hunting for a gas cylinder collar on one — that part does not exist on the 12-gauge Super Magnum. The manual asks the owner to make this identification off the gun, and a catalogue model name cannot make it for you.
steps.caution: On the Super Magnum a barrel seal activator is used for 2 3⁄4" loads and its removal is recommended only for 3" or 3 1⁄2" loads. Note its position before you strip anything, because it goes back in one orientation only.
steps.quote: MODEL 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM BARREL REPLACEMENT: ONLY MODEL 11-87 12-GAUGE BARRELS HAVING 3 1⁄2" CHAMBERS CAN BE USED ON MODEL 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM RECEIVERS.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Important Parts of the Firearm — barrel replacement notice, p.9

steps.title: Operating handle back until the carrier latch holds the bolt open
steps.action: Point the gun in a safe direction with the safety engaged and pull the operating handle fully rearward until the bolt is held open by the carrier latch, then check the chamber and the magazine.
steps.prose: Pull the handle to its actual stop — on the 11-87 the bolt is held open by the carrier latch catching it, and a handle drawn most of the way back will let the bolt run home the moment you let go, with your fingers still at the port. With the action locked open, look into the ejection port for the chamber and then feel up the magazine tube through the loading port, because a shell sitting behind the shell latch is invisible from above. That is two separate places to be satisfied about, not one.
steps.quote: 3. Pull the operating handle fully rearward until the bolt is held open by the carrier latch.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), step 3, p.15
steps.warn: Remington opens the disassembly with it: check the chamber and the magazine to make sure there are no shells in the firearm.

steps.title: Cap and fore-end off, then the gas cylinder collar if your gun has one
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap, slide the fore-end forward off the magazine tube, then remove the gas cylinder collar — but only if the gun has one: it is fitted to 12-gauge models and NOT to the 12-gauge Super Magnum.
steps.prose: The collar is a short sleeve that sits between the gas cylinder and the fore-end and it is the part that most clearly separates an 11-87 strip from an 1100 strip — an 1100 has no collar at any gauge. It is a loose part once the fore-end is off, so catch it rather than let it drop down the tube. On 20-gauge and 12-gauge Super Magnum guns there is nothing to remove here at all, and looking for it is how people convince themselves a part is missing.
steps.quote: NOTE: A gas cylinder collar is used on 12-ga. models only. 11-87 12-ga. Super Magnum does not use a gas cylinder collar 6. Remove the gas cylinder collar. See Picture 12 on page 11.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), note and step 6, p.15

steps.title: Barrel out, held ahead of the gas cylinder
steps.action: Take hold of the barrel in front of the gas cylinder and pull the barrel from the receiver.
steps.prose: Grip it at the gas cylinder rather than at the muzzle: the gas cylinder is what has to come off the magazine tube, and pulling from the far end cocks it in the tube and makes the barrel bind. With the cap and fore-end already off it should come away without force — resistance here means the fore-end is still on the tube or the bolt has run forward. Set the barrel down on something soft; the gas cylinder and the barrel ring are both surfaces that ride on the magazine tube and they do not want burrs.
steps.quote: 7. Hold the barrel in front of the gas cylinder. Pull the barrel from the receiver.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), step 7, p.15

steps.title: The piston stack — three different answers, decided by your gun
steps.action: Slide the gas parts off the magazine tube in the arrangement that matches your gun: a standard 2 3⁄4"–3" 12-gauge takes off the barrel seal and the piston/piston seal assembly; a 12-gauge Super Magnum adds a barrel seal activator; a 20-gauge takes off barrel seal, barrel seal activator, piston and piston seal.
steps.prose: This is the step where the 11-87 stops resembling the 1100 at all, and it is the one to slow down on — the parts come off in a stack and only go back in one order and one orientation. Lay them out on the bench left to right in the order they left the tube rather than dropping them in a tin. On a Super Magnum note which way round the barrel seal activator sat, because its position is what adapts the gas system to 2 3⁄4" loads and the manual shows a specific correct position for it in Picture 31.
steps.quote: FOR 11-87 12-GA. (23⁄4" - 3") ONLY. Slide the barrel seal and piston/piston seal assembly from the magazine tube. See Picture 23b. FOR 11-87 20-GA. ONLY. Slide the barrel seal, barrel seal activator, piston and piston seal from the magazine tube. See Picture 24.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), step 8, p.15

steps.title: Scrub the piston parts dry — steel wool and solvent, no oil
steps.action: Clean the piston/piston seal assembly, and on 20-gauge guns the barrel seal activator as well, with steel wool and cleaning solvent, then wipe them clean and dry.
steps.prose: Carbon on a gas piston is baked on, not merely dirty, which is why this is the one place in the whole book where Remington calls for steel wool. The parts go back dry: oil on a piston collects the next firing's residue and glues the assembly into the cylinder, which is the classic cause of an 11-87 that stops cycling after a wet cold day. Check the seal itself while it is in your hand — a hardened or set seal is a replacement, not a cleaning job.
steps.aside: The barrel seal activator, used on the 11-87 20-gauge and the Super Magnum only, is brushed with cleaning solvent and wiped clean and dry — not scrubbed with steel wool.
steps.quote: THE PISTON/PISTON SEAL ASSEMBLY: (USED ON MODEL 11-87 12-GA., 11-87 SUPER MAGNUM™ AND MODEL 1100™ 12-GA.)
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — component list, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel off, fore-end off, gas cylinder collar off where fitted, and the piston stack off the magazine tube. That is the 11-87 field strip — receiver, breech bolt, action bars and trigger plate all stay in the gun.
steps.prose: That reaches everything routine cleaning needs on a gas autoloader: bore, chamber, the locking notch in the barrel, the gas hole in the gas cylinder and the outside of the magazine tube. Everything past it — operating handle out, action bar assembly and breech bolt out, trigger plate pins driven out and the trigger plate assembly out of the bottom of the receiver — is the deeper strip the book prints on page 15, and that is what the Deep Clean branch walks.
steps.quote: The Model 11-87™ Autoloading Shotgun and Model 1100™ Autoloading Shotgun are gas-operated firearms. Gas operation provides significant recoil reduction by bleeding gases off the barrel to pressurize a piston which unlocks and functions the action.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — CLEANING, p.16

deepSteps.title: Close the action on the handle, then pull the handle out of the bolt
deepSteps.action: Hold the operating handle and close the action, then pull the operating handle out of the breech bolt.
deepSteps.prose: The handle is a push-fit stud into the side of the bolt and only clears the ejection port at one point of the bolt's travel, which is why the action is closed first — with the bolt locked back there is nowhere for it to come out. Guide the bolt forward under control rather than letting the action springs slam it home onto an empty chamber. The handle is loose and small the moment it clears: put it somewhere it cannot roll off the bench.
deepSteps.quote: 9. Hold the operating handle and close the action. 10. Pull the operating handle from the bolt. See Picture 21.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), steps 9-10, p.15

deepSteps.title: Carrier up, feed latch held, action bars forward off the tube
deepSteps.action: Push the carrier release and lift the carrier, reach into the bottom of the receiver and press and hold the feed latch, then draw the action bar assembly out of the receiver and off the magazine tube and release the latch.
deepSteps.prose: The feed latch is a sprung tab riveted inside the bottom left of the receiver, and until it is held flat it blocks the action bar sleeve — this is the step that gets forced, and forcing it bends the latch into a gun that will not feed. Hold it down with a fingertip and the assembly comes forward off the tube with no resistance at all. Keep the assembly square as it leaves so the two action bars do not spring apart where they join the sleeve.
deepSteps.quote: 11. Push the carrier release and push upward on the carrier. 12. Reach in the bottom of the receiver. Press and hold the feed latch. See Picture 22. 13. Pull the action bar assembly from the receiver and the magazine tube. Release the feed latch.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), steps 11-13, p.15

deepSteps.title: Breech bolt off the bars, then put the magazine cap back on
deepSteps.action: Lift the breech bolt assembly off the rear of the action bar assembly, then replace the magazine cap on the empty tube.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt only sits on a block at the back of the action bars, so it lifts straight off once they are out of the receiver — mind the locking block underneath, which is loose enough to shift as you handle it. Putting the cap back on an empty magazine tube is the 11-87 procedure's own instruction and it is a good one: it keeps the cap from being lost and keeps the tube's threads from being knocked while the rest of the gun is apart. Keep the bolt and its locking block together as a matched pair.
deepSteps.quote: 14. Lift the breech bolt assembly from the rear of the action bar assembly. 15. Replace the magazine cap.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), steps 14-15, p.15

deepSteps.title: Both trigger plate pins out, trigger plate rearward and down
deepSteps.action: Tap out the front and rear trigger plate pins with a punch, then lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly, slide it rearward and remove it from the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The pins are a light push fit; a pin that needs real force means the plate is loaded against it and wants supporting, not hitting harder. The plate must move rearward before it will drop clear, because the carrier pivot at the front of it is captured in the receiver. Keep the two pins identified — front and rear are not necessarily the same, and a pin in the wrong hole can stand proud enough to catch the fore-end.
deepSteps.quote: 16. Tap out the front and rear trigger plate pins. See Picture 25. 17. Lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly, slide rearward and remove it from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87), steps 16-17, p.15

deepSteps.title: Safety stays on so the hammer cannot fall
deepSteps.action: Keep the safety engaged with the red band hidden throughout, and never let the hammer snap forward once the trigger plate assembly is out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Out of the gun the trigger plate is a live spring-loaded assembly and a hammer falling with nothing in front of it batters the hammer face and the sear against each other. Remington's own remedy is the safety button you set at the start: with it engaged the trigger cannot be pulled and the hammer cannot be released by accident while the plate is in your hand. Set the plate down with the hammer uppermost so nothing on the bench can press the trigger.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: DO NOT allow the hammer to snap forward when the trigger plate assembly is removed. This can best be assured by keeping the safety mechanism engaged at all times. RED BAND WILL NOT SHOW.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — To Disassemble (Model 11-87) — warning after step 17, p.15

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate assembly: oil only, cleaned as one unit
deepSteps.action: Do not take the trigger plate apart. Spray it with Rem Oil as the manual's Picture 28 shows, leave it for fifteen minutes, spray it again to wash the components off, then shake the excess out.
deepSteps.prose: The two sprays are a wash cycle: the first soaks and loosens, the fifteen minutes lets it work, the second flushes what came loose back out. Solvent is deliberately not used on this assembly — it holds small springs and a plastic carrier dog follower a harsh cleaner can attack. Shake it out properly afterwards, because oil left pooled in the plate drains into the stock head and softens the wood over the seasons.
deepSteps.quote: Spray the trigger plate assembly with Rem™ Oil as shown. See Picture 28. Let stand for 15 minutes. Spray again to wash off components. Shake off excess lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — THE TRIGGER PLATE ASSEMBLY, p.17
deepSteps.warn: Remington: excessive use of a non-recommended lubricant could cause serious function problems possibly leading to accidental firing.

deepSteps.title: Receiver inside, magazine tube outside
deepSteps.action: Brush the inside of the receiver with cleaning solvent and wipe it dry, then clean the outside of the magazine tube with solvent and wipe it dry with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.prose: The outside of that tube is the bearing surface the action bar sleeve rides on for every shot, and carbon there is the most common cause of an 11-87 that short-strokes — it deserves more attention than the receiver walls. Wipe it dry rather than oiling it; a heavy film just collects grit and does the same job the carbon was doing. Take care reaching inside the receiver, there are sharp edges around the ejection port on these guns.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Brush the inside of the receiver with cleaning solvent and wipe dry. 2. Clean the outside surface of the magazine tube with cleaning solvent, then wipe dry with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — THE RECEIVER ASSEMBLY, p.17

deepSteps.title: Clear the gas hole in the gas cylinder with a wire
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off, check the gas hole in the gas cylinder and clean it out with a 1/16" diameter wire.
deepSteps.prose: That one small port drives the whole action, and a partly carboned hole shows up first as an intermittent failure to eject rather than as a gun that will not run. Push the wire through and back out rather than scraping around the mouth, and never open it up with a drill — its diameter is the gas regulation of the gun. While the barrel is off, clear the shooting residue out of the locking notch as well, since that is what the locking block engages.
deepSteps.quote: 8. Check the gas hole in the gas cylinder. Use a 1/16" diameter wire to clean the gas hole. See Picture 27.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Models 1100, 11-87 & 11-87 Super magnum Autoloading Shotguns — Form RD 7061 Rev. 0426 — Lubrication and Maintenance — TO CLEAN THE BARREL, step 8, p.16
deepSteps.warn: Remington: after cleaning, make sure the barrel is free of obstructions.

cleaning.name: BARREL, CHOKE & GAS HOLE
tasks: Correct-gauge brush wet with solvent through the bore several times, then patches until one comes out clean
All shooting residue removed from the locking notch in the barrel
Gas hole in the gas cylinder checked and cleared with a 1/16" wire
Choke tube out, body and threads cleaned with solvent and wiped dry, oil on the threads before it goes back
Never fire the gun without a choke tube properly installed

cleaning.name: GAS PARTS & MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Piston/piston seal assembly (12-ga. and Super Magnum) scrubbed with steel wool and solvent, wiped clean and DRY
20-gauge: separate piston and piston seal, same treatment
Barrel seal activator (20-ga. and Super Magnum only) brushed with solvent and wiped clean and dry
Gas cylinder collar, where fitted, cleaned and kept with the barrel
Outside of the magazine tube cleaned with solvent and wiped dry; action bars with the sleeve attached brushed and wiped dry

cleaning.name: BOLT, RECEIVER & TRIGGER PLATE (deep only)
tasks: Breech bolt brushed with cleaning solvent and wiped clean and dry
Inside of the receiver brushed with solvent and wiped dry
Trigger plate assembly washed with Rem Oil as a unit — sprayed, stood 15 minutes, sprayed again, excess shaken off
Never disassemble the trigger plate assembly
Thin coat of oil on external surfaces only; over-lubrication is exactly what fouls a gas gun in cold damp conditions

reassembly: Check the inside of the receiver first and make sure the link is in position.
Trigger plate: confirm the end of the disconnector is below the end of the left connector, insert the plate carrier-first, align the holes and tap in the front and rear trigger plate pins.
Remove the magazine cap, slide the action bar sleeve over the magazine tube, and place the breech bolt assembly on the block at the rear of the action bar assembly.
Slide the action bar assembly in until the feed latch stops it, push the carrier release and lift the carrier, then press and hold the feed latch and slide it the rest of the way home.
Push the operating handle into the breech bolt.

Super Magnum: piston/piston seal assembly, barrel seal activator (for 2 3⁄4" shells) and barrel seal over the tube, in the position the manual's Picture 31 shows. Standard 12-gauge: piston/piston seal assembly and barrel seal. 20-gauge: piston seal, piston, barrel seal activator and barrel seal.
Operating handle fully rearward to open the action, replace the barrel, then replace the gas cylinder collar — 11-87 only, and not on the 12-gauge Super Magnum.
Fore-end over the magazine tube, magazine cap replaced and tightened, then bore and chamber wiped thoroughly dry.
fncheck: With chamber and magazine confirmed empty: the operating handle pulled fully rearward should be caught and held by the carrier latch, and the bolt should run fully forward and lock when released. The safety button must travel fully both ways, showing the red band on one side only, and with the band hidden the trigger must not release the hammer. Work the carrier by hand and confirm the feed latch and shell latch each return under their own spring. Confirm the gas cylinder collar is fitted if your gun uses one, that the barrel seal activator is in the position the manual shows for the loads you intend to shoot, and that the choke tube is present and tight.
